questions.explanation:
It is important to note that QI projects are fundamentally similar to scienti�c research projects in health care. PDSA involves prediction of the

questions.question_text:
Which of the following provides a method for structuring iterative development of change as part of wider quality improvement approaches
in health services?
questions.explanation:
PDSA is often the central component of QI initiatives. PDSA stands for Plan-Do-Study-Act cycle. Most often in healthcare, ideas are
introduced top-down without adequate evaluation. PDSA cycles provide means to integrate top-down ideas with bottom-up observations
before implementation. PDSA allows us to test an idea by temporarily trialling a change and assessing its impact. The PDSA method
originates from quality improvement studies in the industry. Shewhart and Deming initially described iterative processes that eventually
became known as the four stages of PDSA.

questions.question_text: Which of the following methods of quality improvement focuses only on retrospective evaluation?
questions.explanation:
Root cause analysis (RCA) is a well-established QI method, though some argue that it is mostly a Quality Assurance process that QI. RCA
involves a retrospective investigation that occurs after a sentinel event (usually an adverse event e.g. an inpatient suicide). RCA aims to
identify the putative fundamental reasons (casual factors) explaining variation in performance that resulted in the sentinel event. RCA
focusses on individual events and su�ers from hindsight bias, wherein �ndings may apply only to the speci�c event and not to the system as
a whole

questions.question_text: Which of the following methods of quality improvement is based on 80/20 rule of management?
questions.explanation:
A Pareto chart is nothing but a bar chart but the bars are reorganised to show the categories with most frequent showing events on the left
and the least frequent to the right. Sometimes a line showing cumulative frequency is also superimposed. A Pareto chart helps us to
visualise the high-yield events, which when focussed upon, can result in maximum improvement. (This charting follows the 80/20 economic
principle. 80% of the income of a nation generally goes only to 20% of the population. By focusing on the 20% of high-impact circumstances,
nearly 80% of problems can be managed).

questions.question_text: Reducing waste is a critical part of which of the following models of quality improvement?
questions.explanation:
Lean Thinking is a management philosophy focussed on 4 features (1) preserving value by identifying the value stream (2) reducing resource
consumption by enabling process and value �ow (3) reducing waste and developing pull systems (4) improving overall user satisfaction by
pursuing perfection. Several retail and customer service industries have adopted this philosophy successfully in times of �nancial
constraints.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a consensus checklist recommended when reporting formal studies of healthcare quality improvement?
questions.explanation:
The Standards for Quality Improvement Reporting Excellence (SQUIRE statement) consists of a 19 items checklist recommended when
reporting formal studies of healthcare quality improvement (Ogrinc et al., 2008).
